The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness uses the same symbol (Ra), the same definition (mean absolute deviation of surface height) and the same domain (surface roughness), and explicitly lists si_dimension: L (length). That record therefore directly corresponds to the variable Ra in the ledger and supports the candidate SI vector (length exponent = 1, all other base exponents = 0).

The ledger defines kt as the peak-to-valley height (maximum vertical distance between highest peak and lowest valley). The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height defines the same quantity (mean peak-to-valley or maximum peak-to-trough height), uses the symbol kt among its aliases, and is explicitly described as a height difference (si_dimension: L). This record therefore applies to kt in the original problem and confirms the candidate SI exponents (length = 1, others = 0).

The problem statement names k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface roughness fluctuations. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height gives the canonical quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height', uses the symbol k_rms, and states si_dimension: L. This record therefore matches the ledger variable and supports the candidate SI exponents (length = 1, others = 0).

Sk is defined in the ledger as the skewness (third standardized moment) of height fluctuations. The KB entry pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (third standardized moment), uses the symbol Sk, and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record therefore directly applies to Sk in the original problem and confirms the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

Ku is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of surface-height fluctuations per the ledger. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (fourth standardized moment), uses symbol Ku, and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The record therefore applies to Ku and supports the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

ES is described in the ledger as an effective streamwise slope (mean absolute gradient of surface height). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines mean absolute surface slope (a height derivative in a horizontal direction), uses symbol ES, and explicitly notes the quantity is dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record therefore corresponds to ES in the ledger and confirms the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

Po is given as surface porosity (fractional open area) in the ledger. The KB entry pq_porosity defines porosity (fraction of void area/volume), uses Po among its symbols, and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record therefore applies to Po and supports the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: There are three independent length-scale inputs (Ra, kt, k_rms) and four purely dimensionless inputs (Sk, Ku, ES, Po). Choosing Ra as the repeating length scale yields two independent length ratios (kt/Ra and k_rms/Ra). The equivalent sand-grain roughness ks has dimension of length, so ks/Ra is dimensionless and must be expressible as a function of the six dimensionless groups: kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, and Po. Thus ks/Ra = f(kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, Po).

The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (fourth standardized moment), uses symbol Ku, and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The record therefore applies to Ku and supports the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

ES is described in the ledger as an effective streamwise slope (mean absolute gradient of surface height). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines mean absolute surface slope (a height derivative in a horizontal direction), uses symbol ES, and explicitly notes the quantity is dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record therefore corresponds to ES in the ledger and confirms the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

Po is given as surface porosity (fractional open area) in the ledger. The KB entry pq_porosity defines porosity (fraction of void area/volume), uses Po among its symbols, and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record therefore applies to Po and supports the candidate SI exponents (all zeros).

Choosing Ra as the repeating length scale yields two independent length ratios (kt/Ra and k_rms/Ra). The equivalent sand-grain roughness ks has dimension of length, so ks/Ra is dimensionless and must be expressible as a function of the six dimensionless groups: kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, and Po. Thus ks/Ra = f(kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, Po).
